Residents say consultation process was lacking.

Hackett residents say they were blindsided by an application for a three-storey apartment building proposed for the former SES site on the corner of Madigan Road and Holtze Close.

Login or signup to continue reading

The Health and Community Services Directorate submitted plans to build 27 "supportive housing" apartments on the site, which has been earmarked for development since 2006, in late October.

Supportive housing is a type of social housing where residents are able to access support for things like personal care or domestic assistance.

It is permitted on community facility land, like the former SES site, as long as all the units meet the minimum requirements for adaptable housing, which can cater for all ages and abilities.

Resident Liam Jones said Hackett was a "welcoming and inclusive community" and that many of the residents would be open to a conversation about community housing in the area.

"The problem with this development is that conversation hasn't occurred," Mr Jones said.

Community consultation on the site opened on Thursday, November 5, and will close on Wednesday, November 25, a period of time Mr Jones said was not long enough to consider what he said would be the largest development in the inner north suburb.

Mr Jones said it was clear a significant amount of work had been done on the development application with no consultation with the community, raising concerns that any dissenting opinions on the use of the land would not be considered.

The project has been assessed as a Territory Priority Project, which would prevent any third parties from appealing to the ACT Civil and Administrative Tribunal if the proposal was ultimately approved by the planning authority.

"Lots of people in the community think they should pause to allow proper consultation, proper conversation with the community," Mr Jones said.

"This is community land, and so the community should really have a say about how it's used."

Chair of the Hackett Community Association Chris Mobbs said the majority of residents in the area backed the development of supportive or community housing in the suburb.
